newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt closes down put pares losses.
newsitem.headline: German debt closes down put pares losses.

text.p: German debt markets ended the week with losses but dealers said they remained optimistic nonetheless, especially since the markets had managed to pare some of their losses during the session.
The September Bund futures contract, traded on Frankfurt's DTB, ended down 16 basis points at 102.90 while the benchmark cash bond ended at 102.300 after closing at 103.47 on Thursday.

Dealers faced a session of losses as nervousness had filtered through markets that the Bundesbank might soon nudge interest rates higher, possibly as a first step to counter the mark's continuing weakness.

But economists cautioned that the Bundesbank was not quite ready to raise rates yet, particularly because such a step could threaten Germany's fragile economic recovery and possibly help unhinge the entire intergration process for EMU.

As the Bonn government appears to be enjoying the softer mark, making German goods abroad less expensive, the Bundesbank "will likely not be that disloyal and raise rates," said Gerhard Grebe, chief Germany economist at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt.
Traders said news the contract had closed above 102.75 should pave the way to a smooth start to next week.
The September futures contract traded between 103.05 and 102.62 today and dealers said a similar range could be seen early next week.

But looking ahead further Dresdner Kleinwort Benson analysts commented "even though we continue to be on the way to new yield lows, a correction of Bund future prices to below 101 points should be seen."
Next week U.S. statistics, expected from Tuesday, are likely to again grip the markets' attentions, dealers said, adding the beginning of the week should be relatively calm.
U.S. consumer confidence data will be released Tuesday, new home sales on Wednesday, and GDP for the second quarter on Thursday. Friday will mark the release of July jobs data.
"We will see a flood of U.S. data and we have to be prepared for anything," a dealer said.
